entry.title: Verifiable Settlement and Pricing for Local Energy Markets: Architecture and Deployment on Hyperledger Besu
entry.summary:
We implement privacy-preserving local electricity exchanges using an automated market maker on the Hyperledger Besu network under QBFT consensus. The proposed protocol operator collects individual electricity positions off-chain and publishes aggregate supply and demand on the blockchain, where smart contracts compute market prices every fifteen minutes. Individual positions remain off-chain; Poseidon2 commitments and UltraHonk zeroknowledge proofs, generated from Noir circuits, verify aggregation, payments, and daily balance updates.

Source: arXiv Cryptography & Security (cs.CR) · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #decision-theory #quant-finance

entry.title: How to Defeat a Mafia (of Size 1). The game "Mafia'' is a social deduction game where $n$ players attempt to uncover a covert coalition of $m$ players among the $n$.
entry.summary:
The game "Mafia'' is a social deduction game where $n$ players attempt to uncover a covert coalition of $m$ players among the $n$. Typically, $d=1$ of the non-coalition players are labelled ``Detective'' and have special abilities. Most game-theoretic analysis considers, however, only the variant without a Detective.

entry.title: Bait: Mitigating Harmful Agentic Reinforcement Learning via Probing Reward Function
entry.summary:
We expose a safety vulnerability on nascent agentic reinforcement-learning-as-a-service. Specifically, with a cost as low as $20, we show that safety alignment of a large language model (e.g., Inkling) can be completely subverted through rounds of harmful agentic reinforcement learning (agentic RL) with a toxic environment from its users. We also demonstrate that upon a successful harmful agentic RL attack via the service API, the attackers can potentially use the safety-degraded model to assist with real-world harmful activities, e.g., exploit software vulnerabilities and launch code re-use attacks.

Source: arXiv Cryptography & Security (cs.CR) · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #ml-theory #infosec

entry.title: Attacking UOV-based Signatures over divided power algebras. We introduce a family of divided power wedge attacks on UOV-type systems over finite fields of arbitrary characteristic.
entry.summary:
We introduce a family of divided power wedge attacks on UOV-type systems over finite fields of arbitrary characteristic. The construction extends the characteristic-two exterior-algebra construction of Merz and Ran to the $p$-truncated polynomial ring, where $p$ is the field characteristic. An attack level controls which divided-power relations are adjoined, balancing a lower solving degree against increased average Macaulay row weight.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp

entry.title: Affine Combiners for Reed-Solomon Proximity Gaps. Reed–Solomon proximity gaps establish soundness guarantees for protocols that test received words through random combinations.
entry.summary:
Reed–Solomon proximity gaps establish soundness guarantees for protocols that test received words through random combinations. For length-$n$ codes over $\mathbb{F}_q$, classical scalar combiners achieve error $O(n/q)$ in the unique-decoding regime, with larger known bounds near the Johnson radius. We prove smaller error bounds using affine combiners, which combine two received words $f,g$ as $f(x)+(\alpha+\beta x)g(x)$, where $\alpha,\beta$ are independent uniform elements of $\mathbb{F}_q$.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #number-theory

entry.title: ECLIPSE: Strongly Unforgeable Isogeny Signatures from the Prime-Degree Variant of PRISM
entry.summary:
ECLIPSE is the prime-degree signature construction the PRISM authors describe beside their salted scheme, with that salt, implemented. It exists because a two-dimensional isogeny signature carries an auxiliary isogeny the hash does not bind: the SQIsign round-3 specification says SQIsign cannot be strongly unforgeable for that reason, and PRISM's prime-degree variant has no auxiliary isogeny but was published without parameters, code or a running verifier. This paper is the first implementation, on the SQIsign round-3 primes: a verifier that evaluates the paper's criterion through one isogeny chain and a pull-back, a canonical wire format whose strict decoder recovers one coefficient from two Weil pairings, randomisable keys, two independent implementations that accept each other's signatures, and one key in both roles: a MIKE key pair at the level I prime is an ECLIPSE key pair, the public curve re-encoded and the signing key derived from the MIKE secret alone, with MIKE's code untouched.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #post-quantum #number-theory

entry.title: On the Pitfalls of Modeling Individual Knowledge. The concept of knowledge has been central in cryptography, especially within cryptographic proof systems.
entry.summary:
The concept of knowledge has been central in cryptography, especially within cryptographic proof systems. Traditionally, research in this area considers an abstract \emph{prover} defending a claim that it knows a message $M$. Recently, a stronger concept—termed ``individual'' (Dziembowski et al., CRYPTO'23) or ``complete'' (Kelkar et al., CCS'24) knowledge—has emerged.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #combinatorics
